Portfolio of the product

Built around the way real agent work should feel.

Atelier is positioned as an editor, not a prompt box. The page shows the operating system of the product: context, plan, edit, verify, and report.

Trace

Read the owner path first

Atelier pushes agent work toward concrete files, live handlers, and visible evidence before changes happen.

Plan

Keep the checklist alive

Execution plans move from real edits and stay recoverable when a task is interrupted or continued later.

Ship

Finish with proof

Validation, diffs, summaries, and remaining gaps stay attached to the task instead of disappearing into chat.

System view

Every surface has a job.

1

Open workspace

Files, git, terminal, knowledge, previews, and chat share one project frame.

2

Pick provider

Use the model that fits the work without losing the same Atelier context.

3

Run task

Tools stream in the rail while edits, terminal checks, and plans update live.

4

Review output

The final state records changed files, validation, and unfinished work when any remains.

Capabilities

The editor shell around the agent.

The feature set is intentionally practical: make agent output visible, recoverable, testable, and grounded in the workspace.

Agent sessions

Run Codex, Claude, Ollama, and other model paths from one visible execution surface.

Project knowledge

Index code, decisions, plans, and attachments so follow-up work starts with context.

Diff-aware delivery

Watch files change, review patches, inspect branches, and keep the final report honest.

Preview review

Route running pages, screenshots, console output, and layout evidence back into the work loop.

Tool governance

Keep reads, edits, terminals, approvals, and hook blocks on Atelier's observable tool layer.

Local-first control

Keep workspace state and credentials close to the machine doing the actual engineering work.

Case study

From request to reviewed change without losing the thread.

The product story is simple: reduce wasted model turns by keeping the plan, files, terminal proof, and final report in the same work surface.

FAQ

Practical answers.

Is Atelier a portfolio site or the product?

This page is the public portfolio for the Atelier product: it explains the AI code editor, shows the workspace, and routes people to pricing and downloads.

Does it rely on shadcn/ui?

Yes. Buttons, badges, cards, separators, and accordion rows are built through local shadcn-style primitives under src/components/ui.

Can the download buttons serve real installers?

Yes. The current Next route can be replaced with signed release artifact redirects or streamed files when the release host is final.
